column7: TRIGGER-INTEGRITY-1 item 2 (docs/design/trigger-rowdigest.md, The table the triggers write). The trigger integrity check compared the generation triggers and their function but not system_metadata, the table every generation bump (the check's own included) updates: the server database role could add a BEFORE UPDATE trigger keeping OLD.value, a rule, or forced row level security with an UPDATE policy hiding the generation row, and every bump became a no-op while the check read clean, so a direct-SQL revocation kept authorizing from warm caches (no TTL). The same catalog statement now requires a plain table with no non-internal trigger but the exact retention-anchor one (and, only with storage.database.single_writer, the fence's own triggers, whose guard and callee the fence's census checks while it runs; outside that mode a fence-named trigger is foreign, _SystemMetadataFenceShapedTriggerOutsideSingleWriterIsRemovedAndFlushed_Postgres), no rule and RLS off, with the xmin of each row in the fingerprint; the repair removes them and bumps, and a failed first bump no longer stops the repair. Also _SystemMetadataRuleIsRemovedAndFlushed_Postgres, _SystemMetadataForcedRowSecurityIsTurnedOffAndFlushed_Postgres, _SystemMetadataAnchorTriggerWithoutItsWhenIsRestored_Postgres (all red on main by behaviour), _SystemMetadataUpkeepDoesNotFlush_Postgres. The catalog reads (the check's, the installers' and the repair's) run with search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp only and the server's schema bound: an operator the role creates with argument types that match exactly (an = on (oid, regclass) pointing the reading at a decoy table, PR #3841 fourth review C1) can no longer answer for them (_SystemMetadataDecoyOperatorSeenAtBoot_Postgres, TestTriggerIntegrity_CatalogReadsIgnoreExactMatchOperators_Postgres). The secret_nodes route of #3713 was closed by #3732. Residual: a system_metadata that is not a plain table is reported every tick, not repaired; a superuser below SQL is not detected.
